verdicts.law: A5 / the four-faces rule (never a paraphrase of a sibling; the faces differ in CONSTRUCTION, not vocabulary alone) + entailment item 4 + C7

(a) Against face 0 this is one clause in nominal dress, not a second construction: the same read order (R2 then R1), the same verb 'is entered', the same lexis 'provided/provision against beasts', and the same landing ('as quiet' / 'is a quiet one'); the subject is the only one of the three axes that moves, and the words themselves do not move at all, so the pair does not clear A5's 'past a synonym swap' bar. verdicts.cure: Reverse the read order and re-land the face so it is not face 0 recast, naming the referent in the same stroke, e.g. 'Beasts come to little in the country around {settlement}, and provision against them is entered at the town.' The nominal compression (the variant's density floor, skeleton 2.6) is kept, the order, the subject and the landing noun all move, the referent is named, and no claim is added.

readAloud: Variant 1 [ledger]: the variant lands well aloud and its two-sentence shape earns the second sentence every time; the parent's 'A force stands behind the works' is the firmest close in the pool. Face 1-b is the set's heaviest at twenty-five words and its closing clause thuds on the repeated noun where the first sentence has already done the work; face 1-c's 'A force is entered' is the one opening in the pool that sounds unmistakably like an office speaking, which is what the tag is for.

Variant 2 [street]: face 2-a's 'is up' is the freshest phrase in the pool and the only one that sounds like a town saying it rather than a record stating it; face 2-c's 'The muster stands with the works' has the best opening rhythm of the twelve. Face 2-b is where the ear catches the fault already named: spoken aloud it comes out as a proverb, and the tune gives the maxim away before the law does.

Variant 3 [counterforce]: face 3-b's outside/inside pair is the cleanest read-aloud in the set and needs nothing. The parent's fronted 'Against frontier country' is the strongest-sounding line of the twelve, which is exactly why its unlicensed word is worth naming; the cure costs the sentence very little of that weight. Face 3-c trails past its anchor when spoken: the voice reaches 'and with it' and has nothing to hold, which is the binding fault heard rather than parsed.

verdicts.finding: States C1, C2 and C3 in the ledger's own plain entry with no record noun and no citation (W24). 'the town's works' seats the possessive on the TOWN (W1); 'behind the works' is the key's own conjunction, not a spatial or manning fact; the second sentence carries 'the works' forward (R-i at k = 0) and closes on an OBJECT. No breach found on the card, the bars W1-W27, the label traps or the hard walls.

verdicts.law: W14 (a label at its ENGINE meaning, never its dictionary sense), read against the skeleton's fence 1 AND the skeleton's own section 0.2 (this branch's product chrome is not a licence for the same words in a face); A6 as the consequence
verdicts.quote: The works at {settlement} sit on an active frontier
verdicts.finding: 'active' is not in the entailment table's engine reading of frontier (L-2 gives the middle exposure tier and the unmeasured-town default, and no activity of any kind). Its only two supports are product-chrome surfaces (SummaryTab.jsx:37, threatAssessment.js:74), and the skeleton's section 0.2 rules that exactly this branch's chrome is not a licence for the same words in a face. If 'active' carries anything past the tier token, this face is not claim-equal to its three siblings, which all say 'frontier country' (A6 reads across the faces). Unproven at this desk either way: the marker recorded it as fence 1, an OPEN ROW for the chair, and a refuter cannot settle a chair's open row, so the verdict is WITHHELD rather than FAIL. Recorded as a secondary risk and NOT as a finding: seating THE WORKS as the subject of 'sit on a frontier' leans the word toward the border reading L-2 refuses (the tier is exposure, not a boundary), where the shipped line seated the settlement.
verdicts.cure: Only if the chair rules the bare tier word licensed: 'The works at {settlement} stand in frontier country.' The declared construction, the limb order C2 to C1 to C3, the slot set and the inverted second sentence are untouched. The cost is the pool's one shipped turn kept under 21.4, and that trade is the chair's, not the curer's.

verdicts.finding: States C2 in the office's own formula ('carried as standing', R-vi/W7, a licensed surface with no record noun and no citation), C3 as an elliptical conjunct with 'them' binding to the works, and C1. 'At the town of {settlement}' is W5's naming form. The second sentence carries 'the town' forward (R-i) and closes on a CONDITION. The agentless passive is the form the referent table lists at the RIGHT layer. No breach found.

Then C1, then C2 by W15's second always-safe spelling ('what the town has built'). Carries 'the force' forward and closes on an OBJECT. Distinct from face 2 in subject, limb order, formula surface and close, so the two formula faces are not paraphrases (A5). No breach found.

States C1, C2 and C3 with no slot, as the parent's empty set requires. The street's licensed form here is to state the standing PLAINLY, because no field holds what the town says or thinks (R-iii, R-DA-13's belief-frame floor), and this face does exactly that: no attitude, no duration, no grade, no fused agent (W23). 'inside it' binds to 'the town', which has an outside on every member of the walls bucket, and not to the works, which would assert the circuit D-3 places in NOT ENTAILED. Closes on an OBJECT. No breach found.

States C2 in the street's plainest idiom ('is up' is presence; it asserts no height, material, gate or manning, and stays true of a Citadel and of Gates (if walled) alike because the class word carries it), then C3, then C1. 'with it' binds to 'what the town has built', the immediately preceding noun phrase. Hands 'frontier country' forward to the two modifier positions (k = 2). No breach found.

verdicts.law: W5 (the naming-form article: a frame that needs the generic article to carry a band is a MAXIM frame; state the band as a band) and R-DA-12 (the generalisation test)
verdicts.quote: In frontier country the town has a force
verdicts.finding: The fronted bare-noun tier with no article, joined to a generic-looking definite subject and a habitual 'has', reads as a life-general claim about frontier towns rather than a standing fact of THIS town: the maxim frame W5 names and the generalisation R-DA-12 tests for. The card licenses the row only as a STANDING fact of the record; a maxim is a claim over a class the card does not reach, and W2 requires the tier to be stated over this town's country. The three reads are all present and the rest of the face is sound. The fault is the frame, not the content.
verdicts.cure: Anchor the country to this town's own outside, adding no claim: 'In the frontier country outside, the town has a force, and that force stands behind the works.' The limb order C1 to C3 to C2, the resumptive 'that force', the close on 'the works' (an OBJECT) and the empty slot set are all kept.

verdicts.finding: States C3 by the force's second always-safe class word ('the muster', ADDENDUM 13 A.5 as O-2 re-cut it), and this is the one pool where that word is safest: the force limb is garrison OR militia and EXCLUDES the watch, so A-11's watch-only-town objection cannot arise. It is the CLASS word and not the record, so W24, W7 and OV-5 are clear (no roll, no rolls, no books). Then C2, then C1 by the engine's own bare token ('is frontier'), which the adjacent pool of this same block already carries. 'beyond the town' is seated on the TOWN and not the works, the enclosure breach cured. Closes on a CONDITION. No breach found.

verdicts.law: the card's may NOT: a cause (a purpose predicated of the works toward the country); the skeleton's fence 3 (the counterforce sets the two sides down and settles neither, the reader draws the deterrence); ADDENDUM 8 ruling 2 as the skeleton generalises it (a block's or a key's own name is its name, not a licence)
verdicts.quote: Against frontier country the town of {settlement} has its works standing
verdicts.finding: 'Against' asserts WHY the works stand, an orientation of the works toward the tier that no field on this card computes. The card prints 'relation: (a spine takes no relation)' and refuses a cause outright; the key's own tail 'credible deterrence' is expressly not a licence (skeleton 0.2); and the block's subtitle ('what the town actually has standing against each'), which the draft leaned on, is the corpus's own prose and not a typed field, so it cannot license the word either. This is the weakened survivor of the shipped v3's cause clause ('and the reason is that...') that the rewrite exists to drop. The pool's other three counterforce faces set the pressure beside what stands in it WITHOUT asserting the relation, which is the proof the stance does not need the word.
verdicts.cure: State the pressure as position rather than opposition, one word: 'In frontier country the town of {settlement} has its works standing, and behind them a force.' The fronted pressure, the elliptical second conjunct, the slot, the limb order C1 to C2 to C3 and the close on 'a force' all stand, and the shipped backing conjunction ('and a force behind it', re-seated on the works per W1) is kept intact as 21.4's floor.

verdicts.finding: States C2, then C3 as the pool's ONE negated surface on a PRESENT read, never the opener and one per variant (W10 / R-ii), then C1. The litotes sits squarely inside the counterforce's stance (the absence read against what the tier would lead one to expect) and rejects no alternative, so it is not a contrast needing a named sibling (R-DA-02). 'the country outside' carries no pronoun to mis-bind, the enclosure breach cured. Closes on a CONDITION. No breach found.

The cleanest realisation of the stance in the set: C1 as the pressure, then C3 and C2 as what stands, juxtaposed with no relation asserted between them. The outside/inside pair is seated on THE TOWN, which has both on any member of the walls bucket, so it asserts no circuit, no line and no enclosure of the works (D-6, D-3). Closes on an OBJECT where its siblings close on a condition and on a name not given. No breach found.

verdicts.law: W1 (the binding rule, as this round's own LOCATIVE AUDIT applied it at 3-a and 2-c); W23 (no relation between two referents that no field computes); Part B 21.2 (a refinement keeps its ground only while it stays lawful)
verdicts.quote: and with it what the town has built
verdicts.finding: The elliptical conjunct's 'it' has no reachable anchor. The intended antecedent is 'the town's force', eight words and two noun phrases back; the nearest candidates are '{settlement}' and 'the frontier country'. On the nearest reading the face says what the town has built stands WITH THE COUNTRY, a relation the card computes nowhere and W23 refuses. This is not unclarity standing alone: on its most available reading the sentence carries a relation no field holds. It is also a regression the REFINEMENT introduced, and 21.2's own test catches it, because the draft's face carried no pronoun at all ('In the frontier country around {settlement} the town's force stands with what the town has built') and was re-cut only to move a limb-order figure.
verdicts.cure: Give the conjunct a reachable anchor, adding no claim: 'The town's force stands in the frontier country about {settlement}, and with that force what the town has built.' The demonstrative binds unambiguously; the elliptical conjunct, the set's one A-NAME-NOT-GIVEN close, the slot and the C3 to C1 to C2 order that separates this face from 3-b all survive.

readAloud: Variant 1 [ledger]: the four land as a record; face 0's long country phrase and face 2's office formula are the two that sound compiled rather than composed, and face 2 is the only one not leaning on a negative particle, so it is the one the ear keeps. Face 1's two clipped sentences give the pool its short end but the second starts cold on 'The place', and face 3's 'nothing of works or muster stands' catches the tongue where the rest of the variant runs clean. Three of the four close on an absence, and with 'force' gone from every face the ear hears 'muster' four times across the variant's landings.

Variant 2 [street]: faces 0 and 1 sound like a place talking about itself; faces 2 and 3 sound like the ledger's variant with different nouns. Face 2 trails off on its apposition and has no verb to land on, which is audible — the sentence stops rather than closes. Face 3 opens on the same beat as variant 1's fourth face, so a reader meeting both towns would hear the template before the fact.

Variant 3 [visitor]: the strongest variant of the three by ear — four different ways of noticing (coming, seeing, finding, meeting), no interior and no verdict anywhere, and face 2's turn outward at the end is the one sentence in the pool that reads like a passage rather than an entry. Face 3's 'and the next is' is the weakest beat, and weaker now than in the draft because its tail repeats face 1's.

verdicts.law: THE DENSITY FLOOR (Part B 21.4, read against the SHIPPED sentence) with the skeleton 1.5 'turns worth keeping' and 1.7 'a lost lawful turn'
verdicts.quote: the place stands inside it without works or muster
verdicts.finding: The shipped row's lawful clause 'no force' — the engine's own token at defenseStateProse.js:655, which the skeleton lists as a turn a face may carry whole and whose vanishing FROM THE WHOLE VARIANT it names as the regression ('the ledger's variant is where the engine's own words for the reads belong') — is gone from all four faces of variant 1. verdicts.law: R-i (ADDENDUM 12: a spine's own second sentence carries a noun forward from its first regardless of k) and THE THREAD (owner, 2026-09-08)

Unproven; flagged for the chair.

The sibling shape the refinement cites as warrant is 'nothing of the muster holds them', a definite NP; the bare-plural version reads more mannered, and the refinement replaced one mannered member of the variant (a cleft) with another. Unproven: it sits at the edge of the plain register rather than demonstrably outside it, and it buys the variant its ONLY object close (R-DA-04's varied close kind), which a plainer rewrite would spend.

verdicts.quote: In a country plagued with monsters, {settlement} stands open and unmustered
verdicts.finding: The whole keyed condition in one predicate (grammar V1, the variant's declared construction under W4); the place as subject in the street's own plain shape; C2 and C3 in the compressed positive pair that 21.4's density law protects from being made plainer. Eleven words, the pool's short end after 2.1.

verdicts.quote: Out in monster country {settlement} keeps neither works nor muster

verdicts.quote: What the town holds is the works, and the town's force.
verdicts.finding: 'holds' is possession here, and the block's own landed rows use it that way ('The town holds no works and no muster'), so the siege reading the shipped row carried ('could be held') is not re-opened; the cleft differs from face 0 in verb, in conjunction device and in landing noun (W4/A5); the possessor is seated (W1, A.5); no ownership of the force is predicated.

verdicts.quote: Walls at {settlement} with townspeople behind them, a part-time force
verdicts.finding: Clean. The shipped clause stands verbatim as the variant's density floor (§21.4, ADDENDUM 6); the appositive names what the force is at D-8's definitional grain and adds no claim; the force noun is the BARE plural, so the co-extension of finding A is not reached; 'its' binds to 'a part-time force' (W1); the garrison's absence is carried by what the militia IS, never by its noun (W12, the card's force-class line T-F12).

verdicts.law: §21.4 THE DENSITY LAW (the refinement regression), read with MOVE-GRAMMAR §1.4.1 THE THREAD and the register card's licensed recurrence
verdicts.quote: has walls, and the militia is part-time, drawn from the townspeople
verdicts.finding: The refinement struck 'behind them' and put nothing in its place. This is the pool's ONE face whose two licensed reads are joined by a bare 'and' with no relational carrier; the four other faces that lost the idiom each kept one ('with them' x3, 'and so are' x1). The key is ONE condition — walls true AND militia true read together (R-v) — and the backing idiom is what states it as one. The law named for the cut is R-DA-05 / A11 spread, but the refine's own reserve row records that the gate owns no ceiling on a licensed preposition — a judgment, not a measurement — while §1.4.1 rules A11's echo bound counts FACTS, not nouns, and the register card licenses a word that recurs. A lawful compression was made plainer with no law behind the change. It also leaves 'the militia' an unbound definite on the SPINE, the first thing a reader of the composed passage meets.
verdicts.cure: Restore a relational carrier on the second clause without restoring a claim — 'and the militia with them is part-time, drawn from the townspeople' (the pool's own 'with them'), or the draft's 'behind them'. The refinement's lawful gain ('the militia' for 'the muster', R-DA-10's noun spread) is kept either way.

verdicts.law: ADDENDUM 13 A item 1 with entailment D-1 / D-3 ('who built it', 'who paid' NOT ENTAILED) against D-6's ratified generic
verdicts.quote: and so are the walls the town has built
verdicts.finding: The restrictive relative predicates the BUILDING of the walls of the town. D-6 ratifies the free relative 'what the town has built' as an always-safe generic true of every walls-bucket member; D-1 and D-3 both list 'who built it' and 'who paid' under NOT ENTAILED for the members this key actually renders (the hamlet/village Palisade or earthworks). The table contradicts itself on the point and the chair has not ruled, so the face is UNPROVEN, not refuted. Everything else holds: 'carried standing' carried across by the ellipsis is the office's own formula (R-vi / W7), no record noun and no citation appear (W24), and the indefinite head 'A part-time muster of the townspeople' does not equate the class with the force.
verdicts.cure: Take D-6's ratified form verbatim — 'and so is what the town has built' — or 'and so are the works'; the ellipsis, the formula and the force-then-works order are untouched.

verdicts.law: the licence card's REFUSED COLUMNS ('a totality over persons'; 'an exemption from a duty', whoIsExempt null everywhere), ADDENDUM 13 A item 1 with entailment D-8, and W2
verdicts.quote: the force entered with them is the townspeople, part-time
verdicts.finding: Finding A: a definite plural 'the townspeople' in an equative with 'the force' asserts that the force and the town's people are ONE SET. The recorded rows restrict the militia to a subset — 'Able-bodied residents drill and muster' (institutionalCatalog.js:338), 'Fit residents train and turn out' / 'The able-bodied drill together' (institutionDescVariants.js:442-443), 'A community drawn up for its own defence' (:1158) — and the only row carrying a totality, 'All able-bodied citizens obligated to defend town' (:1344), is the TOWN row, which never generates natively (R-A). D-8 licenses 'townspeople' as what the force is MADE OF, never as who all of them are.
verdicts.cure: Break the co-extension without adding a claim: drop the article — 'and the force entered with them is townspeople, part-time' (the shipped clause's own bare-plural form).

verdicts.law: the card's REFUSED COLUMNS ('a totality over persons'; 'an exemption from a duty'), ADDENDUM 13 A item 1 with D-8, and W2 — aggravated by the intensifier
verdicts.quote: The force behind the walls is the townspeople themselves
verdicts.finding: Finding A at its sharpest: 'themselves' forecloses the partitive reading entirely and makes the identification exclusive — the force IS the town's people, all of them, which the recorded rows (able-bodied / fit residents / a community) and whoIsExempt being null both refuse. This is the variant's numbered line, so the breach sits on the face a falsy seed and the canonical projection draw.
verdicts.cure: 'The force behind the walls is drawn from the townspeople, a part-time muster that turns out off its own work' — the partitive is D-8's own relation ('raised'), costs no claim, and keeps 'turn out', the pool's one shipped compression.

verdicts.law: the card's REFUSED COLUMNS ('a totality over persons'), ADDENDUM 13 A item 1 with D-8, and W2
verdicts.quote: what turns out behind them is the townspeople, part-time
verdicts.finding: Finding A in a specificational pseudo-cleft: the set that turns out is identified AS the townspeople, so the class and the force are again co-extensive over a bounded, specific set.
verdicts.cure: Drop the article — 'and what turns out behind them is townspeople, part-time'; the free relative, 'behind them' (load-bearing here against the ordinary English of 'turns out to be') and the landing all stand.

verdicts.law: the card's REFUSED COLUMNS ('a totality over persons'), ADDENDUM 13 A item 1 with D-8, and W2
verdicts.quote: The townspeople turn out part-time behind the town's walls.
verdicts.finding: Finding A with the definite class as the AGENT of the force's own act: every townsperson turns out. The engine's own surface at this key is a restricted bare plural ('Fit residents train and turn out', institutionDescVariants.js:442), and this face keeps the act while dropping the restriction and adding the article.
verdicts.cure: Drop the article — 'Townspeople turn out part-time behind the town's walls.' Nine words, no comma, both reads, the possessor still seated on the town.

verdicts.quote: The townspeople in it turn out and go back to their own work.
verdicts.finding: Clean. 'in it' restricts the plural to those on the muster, so finding A is not reached; 'it' carries the muster forward at k = 0 (R-i); the second sentence states D-8's own 'raising them takes them off other work' rather than glossing the first (W6); 'their' binds to 'The townspeople' (W1); the fronted locative is the declared construction (W4).

verdicts.law: the card's REFUSED COLUMNS ('a totality over persons'), ADDENDUM 13 A item 1 with D-8, and W2
verdicts.quote: the town's force with them is the townspeople, raised part-time
verdicts.finding: Finding A in an equative. The shipped line's one lawful property (the possessive frame, the two-step order) and the compression 'raised part-time off their own work' are sound; the co-extension of the force with the whole class is the single fault.
verdicts.cure: Drop the article — 'and the town's force with them is townspeople, raised part-time off their own work'; nothing else moves.

verdicts.quote: and behind them is a force of the townspeople. It is part-time
verdicts.finding: Clean. The indefinite head 'a force' keeps the phrase partitive, so finding A is not reached; the pool's one lawful inversion; 'It' carries the force forward at k = 0 (R-i); the standing condition lands last, as R-iv's OPEN is construed on this settled key (skeleton fence 3); 'its' binds to 'a force' (W1).

verdicts.law: the card's REFUSED COLUMNS ('a totality over persons'), ADDENDUM 13 A item 1 with D-8, and W2
verdicts.quote: the townspeople behind them are the town's force, raised part-time
verdicts.finding: Finding A with the definite class as the SUBJECT of the equative — the town's people ARE the town's force. Secondary, and not the ground of this verdict: with face 0 this face runs the same frame in reverse (a walls clause, an equative joining force and townspeople, a part-time landing), which is close to the edge of ADDENDUM 7 rule 4 / W4's construction distance.
verdicts.cure: Put the force on the subject and the bare plural in the predicate — 'and the force behind them is townspeople, raised part-time'; this also widens the distance from face 0, which keeps the townspeople in the predicate.

verdicts.quote: That force is a militia of the townspeople, part-time.
verdicts.finding: Clean. The indefinite head keeps the phrase partitive; 'That force' carries the noun forward at k = 0 (R-i); 'a militia' is licensed outright here (the read IS forces.militia.present, referent table 2.1); the second sentence adds the recorded name and the composition rather than restating the first (W6); the condition lands last.

readAloud: Variant 1 [ledger]: the verbless entry lands, and the office's formula carries faces 2 and 3 — 'and so are' is the sharpest joint in the pool, the whole of the second entry done in three words. Face 1 is the flattest line of the twelve to the ear: two facts set side by side with nothing between them, and a definite 'the militia' arriving with no one having said the town has one.

Variant 2 [street]: 'turn out' carries every face, and read in sequence three of them put the townspeople and the turning-out in the same order, so the four sound closer than their word counts suggest. The nine-word face is the best line in the pool aloud — it lands where it stops.

Variant 3 [unfolding]: the two-step order reads cleanly and the condition lands last on all four, which gives the variant one shape and one cadence. Face 1's inversion is the only line in the pool that sounds spoken rather than filed. Face 3 is the longest of the twelve and its second sentence opens on 'That force', which reads like a clerk going back to make himself plain.

Variant 1 [ledger]: read aloud, three of the four faces land on the idiom rather than the place - "answers a raid on its own ground" comes off the tongue as meets them where it has the advantage; face 2's "turn out on their own ground" is the one that lands as a place, and face 0 runs out of breath on its third adjunct.

Variant 2 [street]: the variant reads as one movement (who turns out, what it costs them, what there is to hold) and that movement is its strength; but three of the four faces open on a person-plural subject and two end on the same ten words, so read in sequence the family flattens into one sentence said four times.

Variant 3 [visitor]: the four openings are genuinely four (finds, sees, comes upon, passes) and the eye stays an eye; the second sentence is the same cadence four times over ("is part-time, not a professional garrison"), so the variant's last beat is where a reader would first hear the machine.

verdicts.law: R-DA-03 (the qualification gets its own sentence, never a tail, never a third); the register card's "a qualification is a sentence, never a tail"
verdicts.quote: on its own ground, in place of a professional garrison, with nothing
verdicts.finding: Three adjuncts hang off one verb and R1 arrives as the third of them; "for it to stand behind" then seats "it" one word after "the town", so the capability clause can bind to the town rather than to the muster. The variant also realises the [ledger] stance in none of its four faces (R-vi's office formula appears nowhere, while all five sibling Invasion & War pools realise theirs with it).
verdicts.cure: Cut R1 into its own sentence carrying a noun forward from the first: "A citizen militia at {settlement} answers a raid on its own ground, in place of a professional garrison. Around the town nothing is built for that muster to stand behind."

verdicts.law: R-DA-02 (a civic LACK is the first half only, stated flat, no completing contrast), with R-DA-03
verdicts.quote: answers a raid on its own ground with no wall around the town
verdicts.finding: R1 rides as a circumstantial on the capability clause, so the lack reads as the completing half of a contrast ("it answers a raid, but without a wall") - the shipped line's "counts for something against a raid" balance restored in another dress. Beside "answers a raid" the idiom "on its own ground" also pulls toward the advantage sense the skeleton licenses only as a place (D-8 NOT ENTAILED: competence).
verdicts.cure: Give R1 its own flat sentence and leave the raid clause unqualified: "...and it answers a raid on its own ground. No wall stands around the town."

verdicts.law: W6 (no doubled beat: a clause that restates the read it follows is the summarising beat)
verdicts.quote: Those citizens stand with nothing built around the town.
verdicts.finding: The second sentence's subject clause restates the presence the first sentence already stated ("the citizens of {settlement} turn out on their own ground"); the beat exists only to carry R1, which is the summarising beat W6 refuses.
verdicts.cure: Drop the restating clause and carry the noun forward inside the lack itself: "Around the town nothing is built for that muster to stand behind."

verdicts.law: the licence card's may NOT ("another civic object of the class force"; "a future"); W25; R-DA-02
verdicts.quote: answers a raid on their own ground, not a professional garrison
verdicts.finding: The contrast is seated on "answers a raid", so the plain reading is that the muster answers a raid and not a professional garrison - the engagement claim the rewrite exists to drop, restored by attachment rather than by wording. The face is also face 0's construction with two synonyms swapped: same subject class, same order of reads (R2, raid, R3, R1) and same landing (A5, the four-faces rule).
verdicts.cure: Seat the contrast on the muster and re-cut the construction: "Citizens of {settlement}, not a professional garrison, make the muster that answers a raid on their own ground."

verdicts.law: W1 (a pronoun after a clause binds to that clause's nearest object); the ambiguity that opens a claim after the spine
verdicts.quote: It comes off their own work, and nothing is built around
verdicts.finding: "It" has "a professional garrison" as its nearest antecedent and the town as its next; the muster it is meant to name is two clauses back, so the licensed entailment (raising them takes them off other work) is hung on the wrong referent.
verdicts.cure: Seat the people as the subject of the consequence: "They come to it off their own work, and nothing is built around the town for them to hold."

verdicts.law: A5 / the four-faces rule (the faces differ in construction - subject, order of the reads, landing noun - never in vocabulary alone)
verdicts.quote: Townspeople make the muster at {settlement}, part-time and in place of
verdicts.finding: Face 0's construction exactly: a person-plural subject plus "make the muster at {settlement}, part-time and [contrast]", then a work clause and an R1 tail, in the same read order and landing on the same noun. Only "The town's own people" to "Townspeople" and "not" to "in place of" move - a synonym swap, not a second construction.
verdicts.cure: Re-cut on a construction face 0 does not use, fronting the two entailments: "Part-time and off their own work, the townspeople of {settlement} make the muster instead of a professional garrison. The town has built nothing for them to hold."

verdicts.law: A5 / the four-faces rule; R-DA-05 (the pool is the unit of spread)
verdicts.quote: and nothing is built around the town for them to hold
verdicts.finding: The face closes on face 0's clause word for word, so two of the variant's four faces land on the same ten words; a face that repeats a sibling's clause verbatim is below a synonym swap, not above it.
verdicts.cure: Vary R1's surface on this face only: "...and the town has built nothing for that muster to hold."

verdicts.law: R-DA-03 (never a tail, never a third); R-DA-18 (the antique air lives in the noun, never in the syntax)
verdicts.quote: part-time and not a professional garrison, off their own work and with
verdicts.finding: One sentence carries four stacked adjuncts, and it does so after a cleft whose copula does not agree with its plural complement ("What turns out at {settlement} is townspeople"); the shape is costume in the syntax with the pool's heaviest tail pile behind it.
verdicts.cure: Break the sentence in two: state the muster and the contrast first, then the work and the lack - "Townspeople are what turns out at {settlement}, part-time and not a professional garrison. They come to it off their own work, with nothing built around the town for them to hold."

verdicts.quote: finds the town's own people at their work and no wall
verdicts.finding: R1, R2 and R3 are all stated; the stranger only finds and sees (W27); the thread is carried by "Those people"; the contrast is seated on the militia, not on a raid; the close is the sibling-licensed contrast in the one variant licensed to close on it (wall 5).

verdicts.quote: are what a stranger sees at {settlement}, and no wall stands
verdicts.finding: A construction of its own (the perceived object fronted), the lack stated flat, and the muster introduced with its antecedent in place ("The muster they make"); no unlicensed claim, no citation, no slot outside the bag.

verdicts.law: THE THREAD (MOVE-GRAMMAR §1.4.1; R-i: a spine's own second sentence carries a noun forward from its first); A5
verdicts.quote: That muster is part-time and not a professional garrison.
verdicts.finding: The demonstrative points at no antecedent - the first sentence names the town's own people, their work and the absent wall, and never a muster - so the second sentence hands nothing back. The clause is also face 1's second sentence with its subject swapped.
verdicts.cure: Supply the antecedent and change the construction with it: "They muster part-time, instead of a professional garrison."

verdicts.quote: are at their own work behind no wall
verdicts.finding: The pool's compressed face; "behind no wall" is the density floor's own compression and is not made plainer; "Their muster" binds to the people who are the sentence's subject (W1); the stranger only passes, which the skeleton names a safe verb.
